records.title: The Rules Are Converging. The Conflict Risks Are Spreading.
records.summary: Five source records connect East Africa’s data and monetary rulemaking with renewed conflict exposure, civilian drone harm and food-supply chokepoints.

records.title: The Dispatch Newsletter
records.summary: The free newsletter and permanent web archive for East Corner and the 39 DAYS living record.

records.title: Amnesty calls for a war-crimes inquiry into shelling that killed civilians in Tigray.
records.summary: The Associated Press reports that Amnesty International independently verified 14 civilian deaths in four artillery attacks on Alamata between 26 and 28 September and called for an investigation of possible war crimes. AP also reports renewed fighting, military buildups near the Eritrean border and conflicting accounts from armed actors; Ethiopia’s government and military had not responded to Amnesty before publication.

records.title: Drone strikes kill 19 civilians in Sudan’s Blue Nile state and threaten power infrastructure.
records.summary: Reuters reports that the Sudanese rights group Emergency Lawyers said Rapid Support Forces drone strikes killed 19 civilians and wounded 20 in Damazin and Roseires. Witnesses confirmed strikes occurred; the RSF did not respond before publication. The group said drones also targeted the Roseires dam and power facilities.

records.title: EAC advances a regional bill for cross-border data flows and data protection.
records.summary: EAC legislative draftspersons, data-protection officials and cybersecurity experts developed a legislative scheme for a proposed regional bill governing cross-border data flows. The Secretariat says clause-by-clause drafting and consolidation are to be fast-tracked by 15 February 2027, with minimum regional safeguards and cooperation among national authorities among the issues under consideration.

records.title: EAC monitoring committee warns that no Partner State meets all four monetary-union convergence tests.
records.summary: The EAC’s monetary-union monitoring committee reviewed the revised roadmap and called for faster implementation toward the 2031 target. It reported progress on the legal framework for the East African Monetary Institute and cross-border payments, but said no Partner State currently meets all four primary macroeconomic convergence criteria at the same time.

records.title: WFP says war-linked shipping chokepoints could add $727 million in costs and cut food aid.
records.summary: Reuters reports that World Food Programme chief Luke Lindberg warned transport disruptions around the Black Sea, Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb could raise WFP costs by $727 million by mid-2027, putting assistance for 7.3 million more people at risk. He said famine risk persists in Sudan, South Sudan and Somalia, while Somalia imports about 90% of its food.

records.title: EAC water data show a persistent urban–rural access gap across the region.
records.summary: The EAC Secretariat said 70% of households across the Community could collect safe drinking water within 30 minutes in 2025, up from 69% in 2022. The regional urban rate was 87%, compared with 67% for rural households; in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the reported urban–rural gap was 90% versus 43%.

records.title: The Infrastructure Is Becoming Digital. The Risk Is Becoming Strategic.
records.summary: Five source records connect water-service data, cross-border public e-services, climate finance, critical-mineral processing and a major airline’s loyalty-programme breach.

records.title: EAC and Estonia’s development agency sign a cooperation agreement for cross-border digital public services.
records.summary: The EAC Secretariat and the Estonian Centre for International Development signed an agreement to support the EU–EAC DEEP Programme for cross-border digital trade and public e-services. The EAC said the work will focus on practical digital solutions, secure data exchange, digital identity, payments and interoperable services across Partner States.

records.title: Africa Day at COP31 puts water security and investable climate resilience at the centre of the financing agenda.
records.summary: A November 19 African Development Bank record of the November 12 Africa Day event says participants called for investment in water, sanitation, watershed management, irrigation, climate-smart agriculture and hydrometeorological systems. The event also identified preparedness for the anticipated 2026–2027 El Niño as an urgent priority and linked the discussion to Africa’s preparations for COP32 in Ethiopia.

records.title: Kenya selects a US consortium for the Mrima Hill critical-minerals project, but development has not begun.
records.summary: Kenya selected the Frontier Minerals consortium, which includes ReElement Technologies, American Resources Corporation and Bunker Hill, to develop the Mrima Hill deposit. Reuters reported that the consortium must still engage local communities and obtain prospecting licences, while two rival bidders said they intend to challenge the decision.

records.title: Ethiopian Airlines investigates a ShebaMiles data breach affecting an undetermined number of customers.
records.summary: Ethiopian Airlines said it was investigating a cybersecurity incident of limited scope involving its ShebaMiles loyalty programme. The carrier told customers that some information may have been affected, said there was no current evidence that financial information was accessed, and reported no flight disruption; Reuters noted that ShebaMiles had more than 5.38 million customers last year.

records.title: East Corner Morning Wire — 19 November 2026
records.summary: Three current source-linked records covering the Rwanda return-hub proposal, civilian deaths reported in West Kordofan and the Ethiopia–Eritrea border buildup.

records.title: Ethiopia and Eritrea amass forces along their border as war fears rise
records.summary: Conflict monitors and people tied to rival militias told Reuters that Ethiopia and Eritrea had amassed forces along their shared border. ACLED reported artillery shelling and armed clashes near Badme, while another militia-linked source disputed that the two national armies had clashed.

records.title: Five European countries plan a rejected-asylum-seeker return hub in Rwanda; no agreement has been signed
records.summary: Austria, Denmark, Germany, Greece and the Netherlands are planning a “return hub” in Rwanda for rejected asylum seekers and are consulting the U.N. refugee agency about human-rights compliance. AP reported that no agreement had been signed.

records.title: Sudanese army airstrike kills at least 13 people in West Kordofan, rights group says
records.summary: The Emergency Lawyers group said a Sudanese army airstrike on Abu Qalb village near Abu Zabad in West Kordofan killed at least 13 people, with women and children among the dead. AP said it could not independently verify the reported toll.

records.title: Ethiopia and Sudan accuse each other of backing armed groups as regional tensions rise
records.summary: Sudan’s military accused Ethiopia of allowing RSF camps, drone launches and cross-border attacks, while Ethiopia accused Sudan of supporting Tigrayan rebels. Ethiopia expelled six Sudanese consular staff and closed the mission in Asosa after Sudan filed complaints with the United Nations and African Union.

records.title: Kenyan farmers adopt erosion controls ahead of heavier seasonal rains
records.summary: Farmers in Kiambu County described using sand-filled trenches, Napier grass, bamboo, terracing and cover crops to slow runoff and protect soil. One farmer said 2024 floods destroyed crops and caused losses estimated at 200,000 Kenyan shillings before she restored the land and changed her erosion controls.

records.title: Africa CDC says Congo’s Ebola outbreak remains out of control six months after declaration
records.summary: Africa CDC Director-General Jean Kaseya said more than 11,200 infections and 5,500 deaths had been reported. He said more than 80% of new cases were emerging outside contact lists and more than 65% of deaths occurred in communities rather than health centres. About $2.9 billion had been pledged, while roughly $1.6 billion remained unreleased.

records.title: South Sudan delays election to February 11, 2027
records.summary: South Sudan’s National Elections Commission moved presidential and parliamentary elections from December 22, 2026 to February 11, 2027. The commission said the extra time was intended for preparations including voter-registration materials, registration centres and logistics.

records.title: Flash floods in Jijiga kill 25 people, including 19 children, a regional official says.
records.summary: A Reuters report carried by VoteKansas.org says 25 people were killed by flash floods in Ethiopia’s eastern town of Jijiga during the week, including 19 children, according to a regional official. The available copy provides the death toll and attribution but limited detail on displacement, damage or the response.

records.title: The Forecast Is Improving. The Physical Risk Is Compounding.
records.summary: Four source records connect a stronger regional growth outlook with fatal construction failure, flash-flood deaths and measurable river stress across East Africa and the Horn.

records.title: The African Development Bank lifts its 2026 growth outlook, with East Africa among the largest upward revisions.
records.summary: The African Development Bank projects African growth of 4.6 per cent in 2026 and 4.5 per cent in 2027, compared with 4.5 per cent in 2025. Its November update raises the 2026 forecast by 0.4 percentage points from the May outlook; East Africa and North Africa received the largest regional upward revisions, each 0.7 percentage points.

records.title: Six people die after the top floor of a building under construction collapses near Nairobi.
records.summary: Police said six people died and five were hospitalized after the top floor of a multistorey building under construction collapsed in Syokimau, southeast of Nairobi. All 405 workers at the site were accounted for and the site was closed. Reuters noted that an October 23 collapse in Nairobi killed eight people.

records.title: An erratic East African rainfall season is already producing localized floods and rising river levels.
records.summary: FEWS NET reports above-average rainfall across much of southern and central Somalia and southern and eastern Ethiopia, with localized heavy rain in eastern Kenya. It records rising Juba and Shabelle river levels, including the Shabelle at Jowhar reaching 5.38 metres by the week ending October 14, close to the 5.5-metre bankfull level, alongside localized flooding in the Tana basin.

records.title: The Alerts Are Specific. The Capacity Gaps Are Already Here.
records.summary: Five source records connect election risk, armed violence, cross-border displacement, Ebola-response failures and flood preparation across East Africa.

records.title: Kenya moves from regional El Niño planning to local flood logistics.
records.summary: Kenyan authorities said 1.5 million people could be affected by heavier October–December rains. Nairobi agencies were clearing drainage systems, identifying 172 possible shelters and planning mobile emergency alerts with Safaricom.

records.title: Ethiopian families reaching Kenya face registration and nutrition gaps.
records.summary: Families fleeing fighting between Somali and Oromo communities in southern Ethiopia continued arriving in Kenya’s Marsabit County. UNHCR had profiled about 14,000 people by November 6, while local authorities estimated that as many as 50,000 had crossed.

records.title: Primary responders say Congo’s Ebola resources are not reaching the frontline.
records.summary: MSF said the outbreak remained out of control despite major international financing, citing unpaid or untrained responders, fuel shortages, weak surveillance and health facilities without basic infection-control capacity. WHO separately said new hotspots continued to emerge.
records.source: Médecins Sans Frontières / World Health Organization

records.title: MVP Build Log
records.summary: The public acceptance log for the NYF Holdings MVP: seven elapsed days and zero accepted deployments before the Day 07 release.

records.title: The Response Architecture Is Moving. The Exposure Is Multiplying.
records.summary: Six source records connect new humanitarian and climate-response institutions with constitutional rupture, cross-border attack and a widening Ebola emergency.

records.title: ADF-linked attacks kill at least 22 civilians across eastern Congo communities.
records.summary: Civil-society and human-rights monitors said Allied Democratic Forces fighters attacked eight remote communities in Ituri’s Mambasa territory over two days, killing at least 22 civilians and abducting at least 10. Homes and motorcycles were burned, and the locations are difficult to reach.

records.title: South Sudan’s December election is advancing without settled confidence in the peace framework.
records.summary: African Union and United Nations envoys warned that a flawed or violent December 22 election could deepen South Sudan’s political and security crisis. The elections commission had not announced party-registration dates and opposition activity remained limited.

records.title: Kenya releases its last Ebola patient and starts the 42-day disease-free countdown.
records.summary: Kenya discharged its last Ebola patient after recording nine cases, two deaths and seven recoveries. No new infection has been recorded since October 19, the last 11 contacts left quarantine, and arrivals from Congo will face a 21-day quarantine.

records.title: Congo’s Ebola outbreak surpasses 11,000 confirmed cases.
records.summary: Congolese government data showed 11,042 confirmed infections and 5,387 deaths across eight provinces. The Bundibugyo outbreak has no approved treatment or vaccine, and delayed detection, conflict and strained health services have accelerated its spread.

records.title: Eight people are killed in a suspected al-Shabaab attack in northeastern Kenya.
records.summary: Two police reservists, five construction workers and a driver were killed in an ambush near a road project in Mandera County. Police and a regional official said the attackers were suspected al-Shabaab militants who may have crossed from Somalia; investigations were still underway.

records.title: African Union and Uganda sign the host agreement for the African Humanitarian Agency.
records.summary: The African Union and Uganda signed the host agreement establishing the African Humanitarian Agency in Kampala. Uganda committed US$86 million in three tranches over three years; the AU said interim staff are expected to move by mid-December and five regional depots are planned.

records.title: EAC adopts a regional El Niño emergency plan with November implementation deadlines.
records.summary: The EAC adopted a joint plan covering early warning, health, infrastructure, food security and climate displacement. It directed the Secretariat to prepare an implementation plan by November 30 and work with Kenya on a regional disaster-information dashboard by November 25.

records.title: The Projects Are Advancing. The Guarantees Are Thinning.
records.summary: Six source records connect regional trade gains and refinery investment with troop withdrawal, diplomatic rupture, trade-preference risk and Kenya’s governance constraint.

records.title: Somalia’s Supreme Court rules the president’s term has expired.
records.summary: Somalia’s Supreme Court rejected the claim that constitutional changes extended the incumbent president’s mandate. It gave political leaders 30 days to agree on an election process, ordered elections within 90 days and limited the government to routine administration while a vote is pending.

records.title: EAC records faster cargo transit and stronger African exports while pressing for trade-finance reform
records.summary: At the EAC MSME Trade Fair, the Secretariat said the Single Customs Territory had cut cargo transit time from 18 days to four and that EAC exports to the rest of Africa had risen 44% to $7.2 billion. Officials called for simpler customs procedures, lower non-tariff barriers, better transport, interoperable payments and wider access to trade finance.

records.title: Kenyan tribunal dismisses challenge to Dangote’s planned Lamu refinery
records.summary: A Kenyan tribunal dismissed a consumer group’s challenge to approvals for Dangote’s proposed 700,000-barrel-per-day refinery at Lamu. The ruling said the petitioner had not shown the project was a public-private partnership; Dangote has offered regional governments a combined 30% stake and targets completion in 2030.

records.title: Ethiopia and Sudan close each other’s border consulates
records.summary: Ethiopia ordered six Sudanese consular staff to leave Assosa and closed the mission; Sudan responded by closing Ethiopia’s consulate in Gedaref. Each government has accused the other of supporting hostile forces as Sudan’s war and Ethiopia’s internal conflicts press against the shared border.

records.title: World Bank raises Kenya’s 2026 growth forecast while naming governance as a binding constraint
records.summary: The World Bank raised its Kenya growth forecast for 2026 to 4.6% from 4.3% after a stronger first half. Its Kenya Economic Update estimated corruption and collusion cost roughly 2% of GDP annually through larger deficits, added borrowing and higher financing costs; Kenya’s Treasury said reforms are underway and expects growth of at least 5%.

records.title: Uganda begins a phased withdrawal from Somalia
records.summary: Uganda began returning troops deployed in Somalia under a bilateral agreement, with the first cohort already home. Military authorities said all Ugandan forces, including personnel serving under AUSSOM, are expected to leave by the end of 2027; thousands remain deployed.

records.title: United States intends to remove Rwanda from AGOA on January 1
records.summary: USTR said the U.S. president intends to terminate Rwanda’s eligibility for African Growth and Opportunity Act benefits effective January 1, 2027. The agency cited trade barriers and concerns spanning rule of law, political pluralism, labour and human rights, and security.
records.source: Office of the United States Trade Representative

records.title: The Systems Are Advancing. The Protection Gap Is Wider.
records.summary: Five source records connect regional digital integration, cross-border displacement, civilian drone casualties and Somalia’s transfer of institutional responsibility.

records.title: EAC adopts regional AI, digital-transformation and biotechnology strategies
records.summary: EAC ministers adopted regional AI, digital-transformation and biotechnology strategies and approved an AI foundation module for universities. They also directed work on Kiswahili AI-certification benchmarks, qualification mobility and implementation frameworks across partner states.

records.title: UNTMIS completes its mandate as functions transfer to Somali institutions
records.summary: The United Nations said its Transitional Assistance Mission in Somalia would cease operations on October 31 after a two-year transition requested by Somalia’s federal government. Mandated functions were transferred to Somali institutions and to U.N. agencies, funds and programmes under an agreed roadmap.

records.title: The Mandates Are Ending. The Pressure Is Not.
records.summary: Four source records connect civilian drone casualties, Somalia’s security transition, financial pressure on Rwanda and competing mediation around Ethiopia and Eritrea.

records.title: AU ministers call for financing that turns digital strategies into infrastructure
records.summary: The African Union’s communications and ICT committee called for dedicated financing for cross-border fibre, regional data centres, internet exchange points, cloud infrastructure and last-mile access. Ministers linked implementation to a Single African Digital Market, interoperable identity, cross-border payments, cybersecurity and data governance.

records.title: Moyale displacement estimate rises to as many as 50,000 people
records.summary: AP reported continued gunfire from the Ethiopian side of Moyale, stranded cargo trucks and an estimated 50,000 people crossing into Kenya, citing the U.N. refugee agency and local authorities. Registration was continuing, and people staying with host families made the total uncertain.

records.title: Drone strikes kill at least 15 people at an Ethiopian displacement camp
records.summary: Reuters reported that strikes on Jari 2 camp in Ethiopia’s Amhara region killed at least 15 people, including five children, and injured 36. Witnesses said no fighting was underway at the camp; the attacker and motive were not identified.

records.title: Russia offers to mediate Ethiopia–Eritrea tensions
records.summary: Russia offered to mediate between Ethiopia and Eritrea on the sidelines of the Russia–Africa summit in Moscow, according to The EastAfrican. The offer came as both governments attended the summit and as Ethiopia received Russian military equipment, raising questions about Moscow’s neutrality.

records.title: The Capacity Is Local. The Shock Is Regional.
records.summary: Six source records connect cross-border displacement, digital trade, public health, conflict governance, war supply routes and food security across East Africa and the Horn.

records.title: Somalia seeks a longer Ugandan troop presence
records.summary: The EastAfrican reported that Somalia asked Uganda to extend its troop deployment as al-Shabaab activity and AUSSOM funding shortfalls increase pressure on Somali forces. Uganda’s State House confirmed bilateral security talks but did not publicly confirm the reported withdrawal-delay request.

records.title: Nyala market strike sends mass casualties to an MSF-supported hospital
records.summary: MSF said Nyala Teaching Hospital received at least 36 bodies and treated more than 150 wounded after an October 26 drone strike on a busy market and a second strike on a civilian neighbourhood. MSF attributed the attack to Sudan’s armed forces; other reporting carried higher death estimates that remain disputed.

records.title: United States sanctions Rwanda’s defence ministry and Zigama
records.summary: The U.S. Treasury sanctioned Rwanda’s Ministry of Defence and Zigama Credit and Savings Society, alleging support for M23 and financial facilitation tied to military procurement and minerals from eastern Congo. The designations block covered property under U.S. jurisdiction and generally prohibit transactions involving the listed entities by U.S. persons.

records.title: The Calendars Are Set. The Conditions Are Not.
records.summary: Four source records connect Somalia's election timetable, Kenya's financing options, Ethiopia–Eritrea diplomacy and regional tourism coordination.

records.title: The Political Calendar Is Moving Faster Than the Guardrails.
records.summary: Five source records connect political transitions, conflict escalation, digital integration and outbreak preparedness across East Africa and the Horn.

records.title: Growth Is Arriving Before the Balance Sheet Is Ready.
records.summary: Uganda's IMF programme talks, oil outlook and regional infrastructure constraints in a source-linked Morning Wire.

records.title: The Financing Menu Is Expanding. So Are the Conditions.

records.title: A diaspora exhibition opens its next public intake
records.summary: Registration opens today for Art of the African Diaspora’s 2027 exhibition at Richmond Art Center. The non-juried exhibition runs from January 20 to March 20, 2027, and registration closes October 20, 2026.

records.title: Private rail capital is following open-access reform
records.summary: Traxtion’s 3.4-billion-rand rolling-stock programme covers 46 locomotives and 920 wagons as African freight networks open to private operators. The company points to corridor investments including the $1.4-billion TAZARA concession linking Tanzania and Zambia.

records.title: Standard Bank puts another $80 million behind Tanzania
records.summary: Standard Bank injected an additional $80 million into its Tanzania business in July. The group reported half-year headline earnings of 26.1 billion rand, up 10%, and expects rate-related pressure in its Africa operations to continue easing.

records.title: A regional AI challenge pairs skills with a prize pool
records.summary: The EAC and Germany launched the second AI4EAC challenge, aiming to skill 20,000 people across all partner states and offering $50,000 in prize funding for teams working on regional problems.

records.title: Germany commits €39.8 million to the integration layer
records.summary: Germany committed €39.8 million in new grant funding after development-cooperation negotiations with the EAC, with the package directed toward regional trade and economic integration.

records.title: East Africa’s growth outlook comes with a financing condition
records.summary: The African Development Bank’s 2026 regional outlook projects East African growth of 5.9% in 2026 while arguing that sustaining it will require smarter financing and structural reform.

records.title: IGAD lays out a year of regional stabilization work
records.summary: IGAD completed internal planning for an EU-funded project supporting dialogue, mediation, preventive diplomacy and institutional strengthening in Sudan, South Sudan and the wider region. Its coordinated action plan runs from August 2026 through July 2027.

records.title: A new dissertation grant funds work before the archive hardens
records.summary: ACASA launched a donor-funded grant for continuing PhD students researching the arts and cultures of Africa and the African diaspora. One or more $5,000 awards will be made annually, with the first application cycle opening in fall 2026.
records.source: Arts Council of the African Studies Association
